Plan, not record. September 2026 has not happened. This is what the planner would do, day by day, produced by the simulator that backtested August to within a fraction of a percent. Forecast demand is marked FORECAST; every declared assumption is flagged in the data. WhatsApp messages are simulated drafts — nothing was sent, nobody replied.

Order-by dates PLAN

Everything the September plan has to buy, with the last day each item can go on a PO before a run slips. At the 31 Aug freeze, 41 of 209 components were already past that day; 47 must be ordered inside week 1. This page is where the plan is won or lost — the build list only holds if these dates do.

The headline case

largest shortfall among the late items
The biggest late order on the board
LOOSE REFINED OLIVE OIL
RM0000001 · loose oil · lead 11 days
The plan needs 6,80,408 L of it. On hand: 30,814 L — 4.5% cover — and zero on order. The first scheduled run outruns supply on 12 Sep; with a 11-day lead the last safe order date was 1 Sep — reached at the 31 Aug freeze. Every day without a PO slips a run.

Chase, don't order

already on a PO — the job is the truck, not the order pad

One item opens the month at physical zero with a live PO already covering the need. Raising another order doubles the stock, not the speed — these are chase calls.

POUCH 1 LTR MUSTARD ROLLS KGS
CHASE
PM0000309
needs 167 kg · on hand 0 · on order 1,000 kg
first landing 3 Sep · 1,000 kg ASSUMED

Inbound basis: Open POs raised in the last 90 days only, OpenInvQty in inventory units, x1000 guard. Where a PO carries no ship date, it lands at order-date + measured lead (oil 11 d, packaging 6 d). ASSUMPTION: lines already overdue on 1 Sept are spread deterministically across the first working week rather than all arriving on day one.

  • Litres / value held are computed only for at-zero items (definition 1). A late item that still has stock — the loose refined olive oil included — shows none; that is a definition, not an all-clear.
